To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the acoustic response to rotor–stator interactions in mean swirling flow is strongly affected by the presence of swirl.

the noise generated by the interaction between the rotor wake and the stator is strongly influenced by the mean swirl, and the noise can be reduced by increasing the gap between the two rows of blades.

the effect of stator geometry on the acoustic response is significant; increasing rotor–stator spacing leads to a reduction in the acoustic response; and, in mean swirling flow, the ray structure of the upstream-radiated modes is very different in some instances compared with the case of uniform flow.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the prediction of upstream radiated rotor–stater interaction noise in mean swirl.
the prediction of the noise radiated from a rotor–stator system in a mean swirling flow.
the prediction of upstream radiated noise in swirling flows, and the effects of mean flow swirl on the noise generated by rotor–stator interactions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the noise generated by the interaction of rotor wakes with downstream stators is strongly dependent on the mean flow, and in particular on the swirl velocity, and that the noise can be reduced by increasing the separation distance between the rotor and stator.

this paper has provided the most comprehensive analysis of the interaction of a swirling wake with a stator row, and that the model is capable of predicting the total acoustic field generated by the rotor–stater interaction.

the model is able to predict the effect of mean swirling on the upstream radiated rotor–stater interaction noise, and that this effect can be significant, particularly at higher blade passing frequencies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the interaction of a wake with an acoustic field in a swirling mean flow is very complex.

we have developed a model which is capable of predicting upstream-radiated fan–stator interaction in swirling flow, and that this model has been used to identify the key parameters affecting the noise generated.
the interaction between the wake and the stator blades gives rise to a complicated pressure field which is a function of both radius and azimuthal angle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mean swirling flow is a significant contributor to upstream-radiated interaction noise and should be included in any prediction model.
the effect of mean swirling on the noise generated is significant.
the effect of mean swirl on the noise generated in a rotor–stator system is significant and cannot be neglected.
